source.text: Μετὰ δὲ πέντε ἡμέρας κατέβη ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς Ἁνανίας μετὰ πρεσβυτέρων τινῶν καὶ ῥήτορος Τερτύλλου τινός, οἵτινες ἐνεφάνισαν τῷ ἡγεμόνι κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου.

records.literal_gloss: After then five days came down the high priest Ananias with elders some and an orator Tertullus a certain, who made a representation to the governor against Paul.

en.L: And after five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a certain orator, Tertullus, who brought charges before the governor against Paul.
en.B: Five days later the high priest Ananias came down with some of the elders and a trained advocate named Tertullus, and they laid out their case against Paul before the governor.
en.R: Five days later, Ananias the high priest came down to Caesarea. Some of the Jewish elders came with him, and so did a lawyer named Tertullus. They told the governor what charges they had against Paul.

es.L: Y después de cinco días descendió el sumo sacerdote Ananías con algunos ancianos y un orador, un tal Tértulo, los cuales comparecieron ante el gobernador contra Pablo.
es.B: Cinco días después, el sumo sacerdote Ananías bajó con algunos de los ancianos y con un abogado llamado Tértulo, y expusieron ante el gobernador su acusación contra Pablo.
es.R: Cinco días más tarde, Ananías, el sumo sacerdote, bajó a Cesarea. Con él fueron algunos de los ancianos judíos y también un abogado llamado Tértulo. Le presentaron al gobernador las acusaciones que tenían contra Pablo.

fr.L: Et cinq jours après, le grand prêtre Ananias descendit avec quelques anciens et un certain orateur, Tertulle, qui portèrent plainte auprès du gouverneur contre Paul.
fr.B: Cinq jours plus tard, le grand prêtre Ananias descendit avec quelques anciens et un avocat nommé Tertulle ; ils exposèrent au gouverneur leurs accusations contre Paul.
fr.R: Cinq jours plus tard, Ananias, le grand prêtre, est descendu à Césarée. Quelques anciens juifs sont venus avec lui, et aussi un avocat appelé Tertulle. Ils ont dit au gouverneur de quoi ils accusaient Paul.

sw.L: Na baada ya siku tano kuhani mkuu Anania alishuka pamoja na wazee kadhaa na msemaji mmoja, Tertulo, ambao walileta mashtaka mbele ya mkuu wa mkoa dhidi ya Paulo.
sw.B: Siku tano baadaye kuhani mkuu Anania alishuka pamoja na baadhi ya wazee na wakili mmoja aitwaye Tertulo, nao wakaeleza mashtaka yao dhidi ya Paulo mbele ya mkuu wa mkoa.
sw.R: Siku tano baadaye, Anania kuhani mkuu alishuka kwenda Kaisaria. Baadhi ya wazee wa Wayahudi walikuja pamoja naye, na pia mwanasheria mmoja aitwaye Tertulo. Wakamweleza mkuu wa mkoa mashtaka waliyokuwa nayo dhidi ya Paulo.

decisions.choice: the high priest Ananias: the same man who had Paul struck in the council (23:2)
decisions.reason: Ananias son of Nedebaeus was high priest at this time; Josephus tells of his wealth and violence (Antiquities 20.205-207). He came in person to press the case.

decisions.choice: orator: a trained public speaker who argued cases in court, an advocate
decisions.reason: The word names a man skilled in public speech. Here he speaks for the prosecution before a Roman governor, as an advocate would. His speech in 24:2-8 follows the forms of a court speech.

decisions.choice: brought charges: laid formal information before an official
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something known to an authority. Here, as in 25:2 and 25:15, it is used of a formal accusation in court.

decisions.choice: after five days: counted from Paul's arrival in Caesarea, or from his departure from Jerusalem
alternatives: after five days of the trial
decisions.reason: Luke does not say where the count starts. Felix had promised a hearing when the accusers arrived (23:35); this is that hearing.

decisions.choice: came down to Caesarea; Jewish elders
decisions.reason: Readable names the place, Caesarea, where Paul was held (23:33), and says whose elders these were.

decisions.choice: a trained advocate; a lawyer
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "orator". Balanced and Readable say what he did here: he argued the case in court.

decisions.choice: un orador (L); un abogado (B, R); comparecieron ante el gobernador contra (L), expusieron su acusación (B, R)
decisions.reason: Tertullus was a trained speaker hired to plead the case in court (meaning decision m2): Literal keeps the word "orador", Balanced and Readable say what he did, as the English "advocate" and "lawyer". "Comparecer ante" keeps the formal, legal sense of the verb (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept at Literal; the speeches keep the tenses of speech
decisions.reason: As for the whole book (1:1): the passé simple is the tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and read in school. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: Tertulle
decisions.reason: French gives Latin names their usual French form (as Drusille in 24:24); Tertulle is the traditional French form of this name.

decisions.choice: msemaji (L); wakili (B); mwanasheria (R)
decisions.reason: Tertullus was a trained speaker who pleaded cases in court (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the word for a speaker; Balanced and Readable say what he was, as the English "advocate" and "lawyer".

decisions.choice: mkuu wa mkoa for the Roman governor (hēgemōn), through Acts 23-26
decisions.reason: The book-wide word, as in John 18-19 and the Gospels: the governor ruled a province, which "mkuu wa mkoa" says plainly.

source.text: κληθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἤρξατο κατηγορεῖν ὁ Τέρτυλλος λέγων· Πολλῆς εἰρήνης τυγχάνοντες διὰ σοῦ καὶ διορθωμάτων γινομένων τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ διὰ τῆς σῆς προνοίας πάντῃ τε καὶ πανταχοῦ ἀποδεχόμεθα, κράτιστε Φῆλιξ, μετὰ πάσης εὐχαριστίας.

records.literal_gloss: Having been called then of him began to accuse Tertullus saying, Great peace we are attaining through you and reforms are being done to the nation this through your foresight, \v 3 in every way both and everywhere we gladly accept [it], most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.

en.L: And when he had been called, Tertullus began to accuse [him], saying, "Since through you we enjoy much peace, and reforms are coming about for this nation through your foresight, \v 3 in every way and everywhere we welcome [it], most excellent Felix, with all gratitude.
en.B: When Paul had been called in, Tertullus opened the prosecution: "Thanks to you we live in great peace, and your careful planning has set many things right for this nation. \v 3 Most excellent Felix, we welcome all this in every way and in every place, with heartfelt thanks.
en.R: Paul was called in, and Tertullus began to accuse him. He said, "Because of you, we have had a long time of peace. Your wise plans have made many things better for our nation. \v 3 Most excellent Felix, we are thankful for this everywhere and in every way.

es.L: Y habiendo sido llamado él, Tértulo comenzó a acusar[lo], diciendo: «Puesto que por medio de ti gozamos de mucha paz, y por tu previsión se están haciendo reformas en favor de esta nación, \v 3 en todo modo y en todo lugar [lo] recibimos, excelentísimo Félix, con toda gratitud.
es.B: Cuando hicieron entrar a Pablo, Tértulo inició la acusación: «Gracias a ti vivimos en gran paz, y tu cuidadosa previsión ha corregido muchas cosas en esta nación. \v 3 Excelentísimo Félix, todo esto lo recibimos de todas las maneras y en todas partes con sincero agradecimiento.
es.R: Llamaron a Pablo, y Tértulo comenzó a acusarlo. Dijo: «Gracias a ti hemos tenido paz durante mucho tiempo. Tus sabios planes han mejorado muchas cosas en nuestra nación. \v 3 Excelentísimo Félix, en todas partes y de todas maneras te lo agradecemos.

fr.L: Et lorsqu’il eut été appelé, Tertulle commença à [l’]accuser, disant : « Comme, grâce à toi, nous jouissons d’une grande paix, et que des réformes se font pour cette nation grâce à ta prévoyance, \v 3 en toute manière et en tout lieu nous [l’]accueillons, très excellent Félix, avec une entière reconnaissance.
fr.B: Quand Paul eut été appelé, Tertulle ouvrit l’accusation : « Grâce à toi, nous vivons dans une grande paix, et ta sage prévoyance a corrigé bien des choses pour cette nation. \v 3 Très excellent Félix, nous accueillons tout cela de toutes les manières et en tous lieux, avec une profonde reconnaissance.
fr.R: On a fait entrer Paul, et Tertulle a commencé à l’accuser. Il a dit : « Grâce à toi, nous vivons en paix depuis longtemps. Tes sages décisions ont amélioré beaucoup de choses pour notre nation. \v 3 Très excellent Félix, partout et de toutes les manières, nous t’en remercions.

sw.L: Na alipokwisha kuitwa, Tertulo alianza kumshtaki, akisema, "Kwa kuwa kupitia kwako tunapata amani nyingi, na kupitia busara yako ya kuona mbele mabadiliko mema yanafanyika kwa ajili ya taifa hili, \v 3 kwa kila namna na kila mahali tunayapokea, Mheshimiwa Feliki, kwa shukrani zote.
sw.B: Paulo alipoitwa, Tertulo alianza kutoa mashtaka, akasema, "Kwa sababu yako tunaishi katika amani kubwa, na mipango yako ya busara imerekebisha mambo mengi katika taifa hili. \v 3 Mheshimiwa Feliki, tunayapokea mambo haya yote kwa kila namna na kila mahali, kwa shukrani za dhati.
sw.R: Paulo aliitwa ndani, na Tertulo akaanza kumshtaki. Alisema, "Kwa sababu yako tumekuwa na amani kwa muda mrefu. Mipango yako yenye hekima imeboresha mambo mengi katika taifa letu. \v 3 Mheshimiwa Feliki, tunashukuru kwa ajili ya hayo kila mahali na kwa kila namna.

decisions.choice: a flattering opening: praise of the judge, as court speeches customarily began
decisions.reason: Speeches to a judge usually began by winning his goodwill. Felix's rule was in fact remembered as harsh: the Roman historian Tacitus says he used a king's power with the mind of a slave (Histories 5.9), and Josephus tells of the unrest under him (Antiquities 20.160-181). Paul's own opening in 24:10 is much more restrained.

decisions.choice: reforms: improvements, things set right
decisions.reason: The word means a setting straight. Tertullus credits Felix with measures that improved life for the nation.

decisions.choice: foresight: careful planning ahead
decisions.reason: The word means forethought. Applied to a ruler it praises his wise provision for his subjects.

decisions.choice: most excellent: a formal title for a high Roman official
decisions.reason: The same title is used for Felix in the commander's letter (23:26) and for Festus (26:25). It was the customary address for men of the equestrian order who held office.

decisions.choice: when he had been called: Paul
decisions.reason: Paul was held in Herod's palace (23:35) and was summoned for the hearing.

decisions.choice: Paul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the man who was called in.

decisions.choice: tú (ti, tu) to the governor; excelentísimo Félix at every level
decisions.reason: One person is addressed with "tú" throughout this translation, even a Roman governor; the courtesy lies in the title, "excelentísimo", the Spanish for the formal title of a high official (meaning decision m4), as for Theophilus in Luke 1:3.

decisions.choice: tu to Felix, even in Tertullus's flattering speech
decisions.reason: French follows the Greek number (style guide §6), as in the tribune's letter (23:30). The flattery is carried by the titles and praise ("très excellent Félix", m1, m4), not by the pronoun; "vous" would add a register the Greek does not mark.

decisions.choice: Mheshimiwa Feliki
decisions.reason: "Mheshimiwa" is the book-wide word for this formal title (meaning decision m4), as for Theophilus in Luke 1:3; "Mtukufu" is kept for the emperor (25:21).

source.text: ἵνα δὲ μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖόν σε ἐγκόπτω, παρακαλῶ ἀκοῦσαί σε ἡμῶν συντόμως τῇ σῇ ἐπιεικείᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: In order that however not any longer you I should be a hindrance, I implore to hear you us briefly in your kindness.

en.L: But so that I may not detain you any further, I beg you to hear us briefly in your graciousness.
en.B: But I do not want to keep you long, so I ask you, in your fairness, to give us a brief hearing.
en.R: I do not want to take up too much of your time. Please be patient with us and listen for a short time.

es.L: Pero para no detenerte más, te ruego que nos oigas brevemente con tu benevolencia.
es.B: Pero no quiero entretenerte demasiado, así que te pido que, con la equidad que te caracteriza, nos escuches brevemente.
es.R: No quiero quitarte mucho tiempo. Por favor, ten paciencia con nosotros y escúchanos un momento.

fr.L: Mais pour ne pas te retenir davantage, je te prie de nous écouter brièvement, dans ta bienveillance.
fr.B: Mais je ne veux pas te retenir longtemps ; aussi je te demande, dans ton équité, de nous accorder une brève audience.
fr.R: Je ne veux pas te prendre trop de temps. S’il te plaît, sois patient avec nous et écoute-nous un petit moment.

sw.L: Lakini ili nisikucheleweshe zaidi, nakusihi utusikilize kwa ufupi kwa upole wako.
sw.B: Lakini sitaki kukuchukulia muda mrefu, kwa hiyo nakuomba, kwa uungwana wako, utusikilize kwa ufupi.
sw.R: Sitaki kuchukua muda wako mwingi. Tafadhali tuvumilie, utusikilize kwa muda mfupi.

decisions.choice: detain you: hold you up, take more of your time
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut in or hinder. Tertullus promises to be short, a common courtesy in court speeches.

decisions.choice: graciousness: a ruler's fairness and forbearance
decisions.reason: The word describes reasonable, considerate conduct, the opposite of harshness (compare 2 Corinthians 10:1). Tertullus flatters Felix again.

decisions.choice: be patient with us
decisions.reason: Readable puts the appeal to Felix's forbearance in plain words.

source.text: εὑρόντες γὰρ τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον λοιμὸν καὶ κινοῦντα στάσεις πᾶσι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις τοῖς κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην πρωτοστάτην τε τῆς τῶν Ναζωραίων αἱρέσεως, ὃς καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπείρασεν βεβηλῶσαι, ὃν καὶ ἐκρατήσαμεν, παρ’ οὗ δυνήσῃ αὐτὸς ἀνακρίνας περὶ πάντων τούτων ἐπιγνῶναι ὧν ἡμεῖς κατηγοροῦμεν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Having found for the man this a pest and stirring insurrections among all the Jews in the world, a ringleader then of the of the Nazarenes sect, \v 6 who even the temple attempted to profane, whom also we seized, \v 8 from whom you will be able yourself having examined concerning all these things to know of which we accuse him.

en.L: For we have found this man a plague, and one stirring up riots among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes, \v 6 who even tried to profane the temple, whom we also seized. \v 8 By examining him yourself you will be able to learn from him about all these things of which we accuse him."
en.B: This man, we have found, is a public menace. He causes unrest among the Jews in every part of the world, and he is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes. \v 6 He even attempted to defile the temple, and we took hold of him. \v 8 Question him yourself, and you will learn from him all about the things we accuse him of."
en.R: This man is a troublemaker. All over the world he stirs up trouble among the Jews. He is a leader of the group called the Nazarenes. \v 6 He even tried to make the temple unclean, so we arrested him. \v 8 Ask him questions yourself. Then you will find out about all the things we accuse him of."

es.L: Porque hemos hallado que este hombre [es] una peste, y uno que provoca revueltas entre todos los judíos por todo el mundo, y cabecilla de la secta de los nazarenos, \v 6 el cual también intentó profanar el templo, a quien además prendimos. \v 8 Interrogándolo tú mismo, podrás saber por él acerca de todas estas cosas de las que nosotros lo acusamos».
es.B: Hemos comprobado que este hombre es una amenaza pública. Provoca disturbios entre los judíos de todas partes del mundo, y es un cabecilla de la secta de los nazarenos. \v 6 Hasta intentó profanar el templo, y lo detuvimos. \v 8 Interrógalo tú mismo, y sabrás por él todo lo relativo a las acusaciones que le hacemos».
es.R: Este hombre es un alborotador. Por todo el mundo causa problemas entre los judíos. Es un líder del grupo llamado los nazarenos. \v 6 Hasta trató de hacer impuro el templo, por eso lo arrestamos. \v 8 Hazle preguntas tú mismo. Así te enterarás de todo aquello de lo que lo acusamos».

fr.L: Car nous avons trouvé en cet homme une peste, quelqu’un qui provoque des émeutes parmi tous les Juifs de toute la terre habitée, et un meneur de la secte des Nazaréens, \v 6 qui a même tenté de profaner le temple, et que nous avons aussi arrêté. \v 8 En l’interrogeant toi-même, tu pourras apprendre de lui tout ce dont nous l’accusons. »
fr.B: Nous avons constaté que cet homme est un danger public. Il provoque des troubles parmi les Juifs dans le monde entier, et il est l’un des meneurs de la secte des Nazaréens. \v 6 Il a même tenté de profaner le temple, et nous l’avons arrêté. \v 8 Interroge-le toi-même, et tu apprendras de lui tout ce dont nous l’accusons. »
fr.R: Cet homme est dangereux. Partout dans le monde, il crée du désordre chez les Juifs. C’est un chef du groupe qu’on appelle les Nazaréens. \v 6 Il a même essayé de rendre le temple impur, alors nous l’avons arrêté. \v 8 Pose-lui des questions toi-même. Alors tu découvriras tout ce dont nous l’accusons. »

sw.L: Kwa maana tumemwona mtu huyu kuwa tauni, na mtu anayechochea ghasia miongoni mwa Wayahudi wote duniani kote, na kiongozi mkuu wa madhehebu ya Wanazareti, \v 6 ambaye hata alijaribu kulinajisi hekalu, ambaye pia tulimkamata. \v 8 Ukimhoji wewe mwenyewe, utaweza kujua kutoka kwake habari za mambo haya yote tunayomshtaki."
sw.B: Tumegundua kwamba mtu huyu ni hatari kwa umma. Anachochea ghasia miongoni mwa Wayahudi katika kila sehemu ya dunia, naye ni kiongozi wa madhehebu ya Wanazareti. \v 6 Hata alijaribu kulinajisi hekalu, nasi tukamkamata. \v 8 Mhoji wewe mwenyewe, nawe utajua kutoka kwake habari zote za mambo tunayomshtaki."
sw.R: Mtu huyu ni mfanya fujo. Kila mahali duniani anaanzisha fujo miongoni mwa Wayahudi. Yeye ni kiongozi wa kikundi kiitwacho Wanazareti. \v 6 Hata alijaribu kulifanya hekalu kuwa najisi, kwa hiyo tukamkamata. \v 8 Muulize maswali wewe mwenyewe. Ndipo utajua habari za mambo yote tunayomshtaki."

decisions.choice: a plague: a public danger, a pest
decisions.reason: The word means a pestilence. Used of a person, it calls him a danger to the community, a menace.

decisions.choice: stirring up riots: causing civil unrest
decisions.reason: The word means uprisings or riots (compare 19:40; 23:10). Before a Roman governor this was the most serious charge, since Rome punished any threat to public order.

decisions.choice: sect: a party or school within Judaism
decisions.reason: The word is used of the Sadducees (5:17) and the Pharisees (15:5; 26:5). It names a group, not yet a false teaching. Paul takes up the word in 24:14.

decisions.choice: the Nazarenes: the followers of Jesus of Nazareth
decisions.reason: Only here in the New Testament are the believers called by this name. Jesus is "the Nazarene" in 2:22, 3:6 and 22:8.

decisions.choice: profane the temple: make it unclean, treat it as common
decisions.reason: The charge goes back to 21:28, where Paul was accused of bringing Greeks into the temple.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the sentence goes on from "we seized" to "from him"; verse 7 is not in the text
alternatives: many manuscripts add 6b-8a: "and we wanted to judge him by our law. But the commander Lysias came and with great force took him out of our hands, ordering his accusers to come before you"
decisions.reason: The longer reading is found in many later manuscripts and was followed by the King James Version; it is missing from the oldest manuscripts. That is why most editions have no verse 7 here. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: from him: from Paul, by examining him
decisions.reason: In the SBLGNT the nearest person is Paul. In the longer text (see the variant) the words would point to Lysias.

decisions.choice: a public menace; a troublemaker
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture; Balanced and Readable say what it means of a person.

decisions.choice: make the temple unclean
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what defiling the temple meant.

decisions.choice: la secte (L, B); le groupe (R)
decisions.reason: In current French "secte" suggests a cult, which is close to the hostile sense Tertullus intends; Paul answers the word in 24:14 ("qu’ils appellent une secte"), so Literal and Balanced keep it for the link. Readable says "groupe", as the English Readable does. The meaning note (m3) gives the neutral sense of a party within Judaism.

decisions.choice: madhehebu
decisions.reason: The word means a party or school within Judaism (meaning decision m3), as the Pharisees and Sadducees are called in Acts. "Madhehebu" is that neutral word; "uzushi" (heresy) would pass a judgment the Greek word does not yet carry. Readable says "kikundi", as the English "group".

source.text: συνεπέθεντο δὲ καὶ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι φάσκοντες ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχειν.

records.literal_gloss: Joined in the attack then also the Jews, declaring these things so to be.

en.L: And the Jews also joined in the attack, asserting that these things were so.
en.B: The Jews who had come added their voices, claiming that it was all so.
en.R: The Jews who were there agreed with Tertullus. They said that all of it was true.

es.L: Y también los judíos se sumaron al ataque, afirmando que estas cosas eran así.
es.B: Los judíos que habían venido se unieron a la acusación, asegurando que todo era así.
es.R: Los judíos que estaban allí estuvieron de acuerdo con Tértulo. Dijeron que todo era verdad.

fr.L: Et les Juifs aussi se joignirent à l’attaque, affirmant qu’il en était ainsi.
fr.B: Les Juifs venus avec lui appuyèrent l’accusation, assurant que tout était exact.
fr.R: Les Juifs qui étaient là ont été d’accord avec Tertulle. Ils ont dit que tout cela était vrai.

sw.L: Na Wayahudi nao walijiunga katika shambulio, wakidai kwamba mambo haya ndivyo yalivyo.
sw.B: Wayahudi waliokuja nao wakaunga mkono mashtaka, wakisema kwamba yote yalikuwa hivyo.
sw.R: Wayahudi waliokuwepo walikubaliana na Tertulo. Walisema kwamba yote hayo yalikuwa kweli.

decisions.choice: joined in the attack: joined in pressing the charge
decisions.reason: The verb means to join in attacking someone. Here the others took up the accusation with Tertullus.

decisions.choice: the Jews who had come; who were there
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that these are the high priest and elders of 24:1.

source.text: Ἀπεκρίθη τε ὁ Παῦλος νεύσαντος αὐτῷ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος λέγειν· Ἐκ πολλῶν ἐτῶν ὄντα σε κριτὴν τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ ἐπιστάμενος εὐθύμως τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ἀπολογοῦμαι, δυναμένου σου ἐπιγνῶναι, ὅτι οὐ πλείους εἰσίν μοι ἡμέραι δώδεκα ἀφ’ ἧς ἀνέβην προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, καὶ οὔτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ εὗρόν με πρός τινα διαλεγόμενον ἢ ἐπίστασιν ποιοῦντα ὄχλου οὔτε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς οὔτε κατὰ τὴν πόλιν, οὐδὲ παραστῆσαι δύνανταί σοι περὶ ὧν νυνὶ κατηγοροῦσίν μου.

records.literal_gloss: Answered then Paul, having nodded to him the governor to speak, For many years being you judge to the nation this knowing, cheerfully the things concerning myself I make a defense, \v 11 being able you to know that not more there are to me days twelve from which I went up to worship in Jerusalem, \v 12 and neither in the temple did they find me with anyone reasoning or a gathering making of a crowd, nor in the synagogues nor in the city, \v 13 nor to prove to you are they able concerning [the things] of which now they accuse me.

en.L: And when the governor had nodded to him to speak, Paul answered, "Knowing that for many years you have been a judge to this nation, I cheerfully make my defense concerning myself, \v 11 since you are able to learn that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship in Jerusalem. \v 12 And neither in the temple did they find me arguing with anyone or causing a crowd to gather, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city. \v 13 Nor are they able to prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.
en.B: The governor signaled to Paul to speak, and he answered: "You have judged this nation for many years, and knowing that, I am glad to answer for myself before you. \v 11 It is only twelve days, no more, since I went up to Jerusalem to worship, as you can find out. \v 12 They never found me in the temple in debate with anyone or drawing a crowd together, nor in the synagogues, nor anywhere in the city. \v 13 They have no proof to set before you for the things they now charge me with.
en.R: Then the governor nodded to Paul, to show that he could speak. Paul said, "You have been a judge over this nation for many years. So I am glad to speak to you and defend myself. \v 11 You can check this for yourself: only twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship God. \v 12 These people did not find me arguing with anyone in the temple. They did not see me stirring up a crowd in the synagogues or anywhere else in the city. \v 13 They cannot prove any of the things they say against me.

es.L: Y respondió Pablo, después de que el gobernador le hiciera señas para que hablara: «Sabiendo que desde hace muchos años eres juez de esta nación, con buen ánimo presento la defensa de lo que a mí respecta, \v 11 pudiendo tú comprobar que no hace más de doce días que subí a adorar a Jerusalén. \v 12 Y ni en el templo me hallaron discutiendo con nadie o provocando una aglomeración de gente, ni en las sinagogas, ni por la ciudad. \v 13 Tampoco pueden probarte las cosas de las que ahora me acusan.
es.B: El gobernador le hizo una señal a Pablo para que hablara, y él respondió: «Sé que hace muchos años que eres juez de esta nación, y por eso me defiendo ante ti de buena gana. \v 11 Solo han pasado doce días, no más, desde que subí a Jerusalén para adorar, como puedes comprobar. \v 12 Nunca me encontraron en el templo discutiendo con nadie ni reuniendo a la multitud, ni en las sinagogas, ni en ningún lugar de la ciudad. \v 13 No tienen pruebas que presentarte de lo que ahora me acusan.
es.R: Entonces el gobernador le hizo una señal con la cabeza a Pablo para indicarle que podía hablar. Pablo dijo: «Tú has sido juez de esta nación durante muchos años. Por eso me alegra hablar contigo y defenderme. \v 11 Puedes comprobarlo tú mismo: hace solo doce días subí a Jerusalén para adorar a Dios. \v 12 Esta gente no me encontró discutiendo con nadie en el templo. Tampoco me vieron alborotando a la gente en las sinagogas ni en ningún otro lugar de la ciudad. \v 13 No pueden probar nada de lo que dicen contra mí.

fr.L: Et Paul répondit, le gouverneur lui ayant fait signe de parler : « Sachant que depuis de nombreuses années tu es juge pour cette nation, c’est de bon cœur que je présente ma défense en ce qui me concerne, \v 11 puisque tu peux t’assurer qu’il n’y a pas plus de douze jours que je suis monté adorer à Jérusalem. \v 12 Et ils ne m’ont trouvé ni dans le temple en train de discuter avec quelqu’un ou de provoquer un attroupement de la foule, ni dans les synagogues, ni dans la ville. \v 13 Et ils ne peuvent pas non plus te prouver ce dont ils m’accusent maintenant.
fr.B: Le gouverneur fit signe à Paul de parler, et celui-ci répondit : « Je sais que tu juges cette nation depuis de nombreuses années ; c’est donc de bon cœur que je présente ma défense devant toi. \v 11 Il n’y a que douze jours, pas davantage, que je suis monté à Jérusalem pour adorer, comme tu peux le vérifier. \v 12 On ne m’a jamais trouvé dans le temple en train de débattre avec quelqu’un ou d’ameuter la foule, ni dans les synagogues, ni nulle part dans la ville. \v 13 Ils n’ont aucune preuve à te présenter de ce dont ils m’accusent maintenant.
fr.R: Alors le gouverneur a fait un signe de tête à Paul pour lui montrer qu’il pouvait parler. Paul a dit : « Tu es juge de cette nation depuis de nombreuses années. Je suis donc content de te parler et de me défendre. \v 11 Tu peux le vérifier toi-même : il y a seulement douze jours, je suis monté à Jérusalem pour adorer Dieu. \v 12 Ces gens ne m’ont pas trouvé dans le temple en train de me disputer avec quelqu’un. Ils ne m’ont pas vu exciter la foule dans les synagogues, ni ailleurs dans la ville. \v 13 Ils ne peuvent prouver aucune des choses qu’ils disent contre moi.

sw.L: Na Paulo alijibu, mkuu wa mkoa alipokwisha kumwashiria kwa kichwa aseme, "Nikijua kwamba kwa miaka mingi wewe umekuwa hakimu wa taifa hili, ninajitetea kwa moyo mkunjufu kuhusu mambo yangu, \v 11 kwa kuwa wewe unaweza kujua kwamba hazijapita siku zaidi ya kumi na mbili tangu nilipopanda kwenda kuabudu Yerusalemu. \v 12 Na hawakuniona hekaluni nikibishana na mtu yeyote au nikikusanya umati wa watu, wala katika masinagogi, wala mjini. \v 13 Wala hawawezi kukuthibitishia mambo wanayonishtaki sasa.
sw.B: Mkuu wa mkoa alimwashiria Paulo aseme, naye akajibu, "Najua kwamba umekuwa hakimu wa taifa hili kwa miaka mingi, kwa hiyo ninajitetea mbele yako kwa furaha. \v 11 Ni siku kumi na mbili tu, si zaidi, tangu nilipopanda Yerusalemu kuabudu, kama unavyoweza kuthibitisha. \v 12 Hawakuniona hekaluni nikibishana na mtu yeyote wala nikikusanya umati, wala katika masinagogi, wala popote mjini. \v 13 Hawana ushahidi wa kukuletea juu ya mambo wanayonishtaki sasa.
sw.R: Kisha mkuu wa mkoa akamwashiria Paulo kwa kichwa kwamba anaweza kusema. Paulo akasema, "Wewe umekuwa hakimu wa taifa hili kwa miaka mingi. Kwa hiyo nafurahi kuzungumza nawe na kujitetea. \v 11 Unaweza kuchunguza jambo hili wewe mwenyewe: ni siku kumi na mbili tu tangu nilipopanda Yerusalemu kumwabudu Mungu. \v 12 Watu hawa hawakuniona nikibishana na mtu yeyote hekaluni. Hawakuniona nikichochea umati wa watu katika masinagogi, wala mahali pengine popote mjini. \v 13 Hawawezi kuthibitisha jambo lolote kati ya yale wanayosema dhidi yangu.

decisions.choice: Paul's opening: a courteous but plain appeal to the judge's experience
decisions.reason: Paul also opens by addressing the judge, as court speeches did, but he praises nothing. He only says that Felix has long experience of the Jewish nation and so can judge these matters. Felix had governed Judea for some years by now.

decisions.choice: not more than twelve days: since Paul arrived in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Counting from his arrival (21:17), Paul had spent only a few days in the city before his arrest. The short time makes the charge of stirring up riots across the world look unlikely.

decisions.choice: arguing: discussing, debating
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of Paul's discussions in synagogues (17:2; 18:4; 19:8). He says he did not even do that in Jerusalem this time.

decisions.choice: causing a crowd to gather: stirring up a mob
decisions.reason: The noun means a gathering together, here of a crowd. Paul answers the charge of 24:5 directly.

decisions.choice: prove: set out evidence for
decisions.reason: The verb means to present or establish. The accusers bring charges but no proof.

decisions.choice: to worship God
decisions.reason: Readable names the one Paul came to worship.

decisions.choice: It is only twelve days ... as you can find out
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the fact first and the appeal to Felix's knowledge after it, to make a shorter English sentence.

source.text: ὁμολογῶ δὲ τοῦτό σοι ὅτι κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἣν λέγουσιν αἵρεσιν οὕτως λατρεύω τῷ πατρῴῳ θεῷ, πιστεύων πᾶσι τοῖς κατὰ τὸν νόμον καὶ τοῖς ἐν τοῖς προφήταις γεγραμμένοις, ἐλπίδα ἔχων εἰς τὸν θεόν, ἣν καὶ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι προσδέχονται, ἀνάστασιν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι δικαίων τε καὶ ἀδίκων·

records.literal_gloss: I confess however this to you, that according to the Way which they call a sect, so I serve the ancestral God, believing all things according to the law and that in the Prophets have been written, \v 15 a hope having toward God, which also these themselves await, a resurrection to be about to be of both righteous and unrighteous.

en.L: But this I confess to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of [our] fathers, believing everything that accords with the law and that is written in the Prophets, \v 15 having a hope in God, which these men themselves also await, that there is going to be a resurrection of both [the] righteous and [the] unrighteous.
en.B: This much I do acknowledge before you: it is as one who follows the Way, which they call a sect, that I serve the God of our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}. I believe all that accords with the law and all that stands written in the Prophets. \v 15 My hope rests on God, and these men look for it too: that a resurrection is coming, of the righteous and the unrighteous alike.
en.R: But I will tell you this. I follow the Way. They call it a sect, but in this Way I worship the God of our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}. I believe everything that the law says and everything that is written in the books of the prophets. \v 15 I trust God, and I have the same hope these men have: God will raise the dead to life, both those who did right and those who did wrong.

es.L: Pero esto te confieso: que según el Camino, al que llaman secta, así sirvo al Dios de [nuestros] padres, creyendo todo lo que es conforme a la ley y lo que está escrito en los Profetas, \v 15 teniendo una esperanza en Dios, la cual también estos mismos aguardan: que va a haber una resurrección tanto de justos como de injustos.
es.B: Esto sí lo reconozco ante ti: es como seguidor del Camino, al que ellos llaman secta, como sirvo al Dios de nuestros {{gender:antepasados|padres}}. Creo todo lo que concuerda con la ley y todo lo que está escrito en los Profetas. \v 15 Mi esperanza está puesta en Dios, y estos hombres también la aguardan: que habrá una resurrección, tanto de los justos como de los injustos.
es.R: Pero te digo esto: yo sigo el Camino. Ellos lo llaman secta, pero en este Camino yo adoro al Dios de nuestros {{gender:antepasados|padres}}. Creo todo lo que dice la ley y todo lo que está escrito en los libros de los profetas. \v 15 Confío en Dios, y tengo la misma esperanza que tienen estos hombres: Dios resucitará a los muertos, tanto a los que hicieron el bien como a los que hicieron el mal.

fr.L: Mais je te reconnais ceci : selon la Voie, qu’ils appellent une secte, c’est ainsi que je sers le Dieu de [nos] pères, croyant tout ce qui est conforme à la Loi et ce qui est écrit dans les Prophètes, \v 15 ayant en Dieu une espérance que ceux-ci eux-mêmes attendent aussi : qu’il va y avoir une résurrection des justes et des injustes.
fr.B: Je te le reconnais pourtant : c’est en suivant la Voie, qu’ils appellent une secte, que je sers le Dieu de nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. Je crois tout ce qui est conforme à la Loi et tout ce qui est écrit dans les Prophètes. \v 15 Mon espérance repose sur Dieu, et ces hommes l’attendent aussi : une résurrection va venir, celle des justes comme des injustes.
fr.R: Mais je vais te dire une chose. Je fais partie de ceux qui suivent la Voie. Ils l’appellent une secte, mais c’est en suivant cette Voie que j’adore le Dieu de nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. Je crois tout ce que dit la Loi et tout ce qui est écrit dans les livres des prophètes. \v 15 J’ai confiance en Dieu, et j’ai la même espérance que ces hommes : Dieu fera revivre les morts, ceux qui ont fait le bien et ceux qui ont fait le mal.

sw.L: Lakini hili nakiri kwako, kwamba kwa kufuata ile Njia, wanayoiita madhehebu, ndivyo ninavyomtumikia Mungu wa baba [zetu], nikiamini yote yaliyo kulingana na sheria na yaliyoandikwa katika Manabii, \v 15 nikiwa na tumaini kwa Mungu, ambalo hawa wenyewe nao wanalingojea, kwamba kutakuwa na ufufuo wa wenye haki na wasio na haki pia.
sw.B: Lakini hili nakiri mbele yako: ninamtumikia Mungu wa {{gender:wahenga|mababu}} wetu kama mfuasi wa ile Njia, ambayo wao wanaiita madhehebu. Ninaamini yote yanayokubaliana na sheria na yote yaliyoandikwa katika Manabii. \v 15 Tumaini langu liko kwa Mungu, na watu hawa nao wanalitazamia: kwamba kutakuwa na ufufuo wa wenye haki na wa waovu pia.
sw.R: Lakini nakuambia hili: mimi ninaifuata ile Njia. Wao wanaiita madhehebu, lakini katika Njia hii mimi ninamwabudu Mungu wa {{gender:wahenga|mababu}} wetu. Ninaamini kila kitu ambacho sheria inasema, na kila kitu kilichoandikwa katika vitabu vya manabii. \v 15 Ninamtumaini Mungu, na nina tumaini lile lile walilo nalo watu hawa: Mungu atawafufua wafu, wale waliotenda mema na wale waliotenda mabaya.

decisions.choice: the Way: the movement of those who follow Jesus
alternatives: a way of life in general
decisions.reason: Luke uses this name for the believers in 9:2, 19:9, 19:23 and 22:4. Paul uses it in place of the word his accusers chose.

decisions.choice: a sect: a party that splits off
decisions.reason: Tertullus used the word in 24:5. Paul does not accept it as a fair name: he worships the same God and holds the same Scriptures. The word could be neutral (26:5), but here it is the accusers' label.

decisions.choice: serve: worship God with religious service
decisions.reason: The verb is used of worship and service given to God (7:7; 26:7; 27:23).

decisions.choice: the God of our fathers: the God of Israel's forebears
decisions.reason: The adjective means inherited from the fathers. Paul claims continuity with Israel's faith (compare 3:13; 5:30; 22:14).

decisions.choice: the law and the Prophets: the Scriptures of Israel
decisions.reason: The law and the Prophets were two parts of the Hebrew Scriptures, and the phrase stands for the whole (13:15; 28:23).

decisions.choice: a resurrection of the righteous and the unrighteous: all the dead will be raised for judgment
decisions.reason: Daniel 12:2 speaks of many rising, some to life and some to shame, and Jesus says the same in John 5:28-29. The word for righteous here is the adjective for people who are just, not the noun righteousness in 24:25.

decisions.choice: which these men themselves also await: the hope held by Paul's Jewish accusers
decisions.reason: Many Jews, the Pharisees above all, hoped for the resurrection (23:6-8). The Sadducees denied it, so Paul speaks of what his people hold in general, not of every person present.

decisions.choice: those who did right and those who did wrong
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two groups in plain words.

decisions.choice: God will raise the dead to life
alternatives: a resurrection is going to be
decisions.reason: Readable says what the resurrection is and who brings it about.

decisions.choice: el Camino, with a capital; secta
decisions.reason: "The Way" is the name of the movement of those who follow Jesus (meaning decision m1), so it takes a capital, as in English. "Secta" is the accusers' word (meaning decision m2); Paul quotes it and does not accept it.

decisions.choice: Je fais partie de ceux qui suivent la Voie
decisions.reason: The English Readable "I follow the Way" would be "Je suis la Voie" in French, which also reads "I am the Way" (John 14:6), so Readable says it another way.

decisions.choice: ile Njia, with a capital
decisions.reason: "The Way" is the name of the movement of those who follow Jesus (meaning decision m1), so it takes a capital, and "ile" marks it as the Way already known in Acts. The gender span follows the English and John 6:58 ("wahenga", "mababu").

source.text: ἐν τούτῳ καὶ αὐτὸς ἀσκῶ ἀπρόσκοπον συνείδησιν ἔχειν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους διὰ παντός.

records.literal_gloss: In this also I myself strive without offense a conscience to have toward God and men through everything.

en.L: In this I myself also strive always to have a conscience without offense toward God and {{gender:people|men}}.
en.B: That is why I, for my part, take pains to live with a blameless conscience toward God and toward people at all times.
en.R: Because of this hope, I always try hard to do what is right before God and before people. Then my conscience does not blame me for anything.

es.L: En esto también yo mismo me ejercito para tener una conciencia sin tropiezo delante de Dios y de {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} en todo momento.
es.B: Por eso yo, por mi parte, me empeño en vivir siempre con la conciencia limpia delante de Dios y delante de la gente.
es.R: Por esta esperanza, siempre trato con todas mis fuerzas de hacer lo correcto delante de Dios y delante de la gente. Así mi conciencia no me acusa de nada.

fr.L: En cela, moi aussi, je m’exerce à avoir toujours une conscience sans reproche envers Dieu et envers {{gender:les humains|les hommes}}.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi, de mon côté, je m’efforce d’avoir en tout temps une conscience irréprochable devant Dieu et devant {{gender:les humains|les hommes}}.
fr.R: À cause de cette espérance, je fais toujours de mon mieux pour faire ce qui est juste devant Dieu et devant les autres. Ainsi, ma conscience ne me reproche rien.

sw.L: Katika hili mimi mwenyewe pia najitahidi kuwa na dhamiri isiyo na lawama mbele ya Mungu na mbele ya watu daima.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu mimi, kwa upande wangu, najibidiisha kuishi kila wakati na dhamiri safi mbele ya Mungu na mbele ya watu.
sw.R: Kwa sababu ya tumaini hili, mimi hujitahidi sana kila wakati kutenda yaliyo sawa mbele ya Mungu na mbele ya watu. Hivyo dhamiri yangu hainilaumu kwa jambo lolote.

decisions.choice: in this: because of this hope
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely looks back to the hope of the resurrection and the judgment it brings. It could also mean "meanwhile" or "in this way of life".

decisions.choice: a conscience without offense: one that has nothing to accuse
alternatives: a conscience that causes no one to stumble
decisions.reason: The adjective means not stumbling or not giving offense. Paul says something similar before the council in 23:1.

decisions.choice: because of this hope
decisions.reason: Readable says what "this" refers to, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: try hard to do what is right ... my conscience does not blame me
alternatives: strive to have a conscience without offense
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a clear conscience means in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: {{gender:les humains|les hommes}} (B); les autres, no setting (R)
alternatives: les gens at Balanced, no setting
decisions.reason: English Balanced says "people" without a setting; French must choose between "les humains" and the traditional generic "les hommes", so Balanced carries the setting as Literal does. Readable says "les autres", which is already inclusive.

source.text: δι’ ἐτῶν δὲ πλειόνων ἐλεημοσύνας ποιήσων εἰς τὸ ἔθνος μου παρεγενόμην καὶ προσφοράς, ἐν αἷς εὗρόν με ἡγνισμένον ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, οὐ μετὰ ὄχλου οὐδὲ μετὰ θορύβου, τινὲς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι, οὓς ἔδει ἐπὶ σοῦ παρεῖναι καὶ κατηγορεῖν εἴ τι ἔχοιεν πρὸς ἐμέ, ἢ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι εἰπάτωσαν τί εὗρον ἀδίκημα στάντος μου ἐπὶ τοῦ συνεδρίου ἢ περὶ μιᾶς ταύτης φωνῆς ἧς ἐκέκραξα ἐν αὐτοῖς ἑστὼς ὅτι Περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ἐγὼ κρίνομαι σήμερον ἐφ’ ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: After years now several alms to bring to the nation of me I arrived and offerings, \v 18 in which they found me purified in the temple, not with a crowd nor with tumult, \v 19 some however from Asia Jews, who ought before you to be present and to accuse, if anything they may have against me; \v 20 or these themselves let them say what they found wrongdoing, having stood me before the council, \v 21 or concerning one this voice which I cried out among them standing, that Concerning resurrection of dead I am judged today by you.

en.L: Now after several years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings, \v 18 in the course of which they found me purified in the temple, not with a crowd nor with an uproar. \v 19 But [there were] some Jews from Asia, who ought to be present before you and to accuse [me], if they should have anything against me. \v 20 Or let these men themselves say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the council, \v 21 other than about this one statement which I cried out while standing among them: 'Concerning [the] resurrection of [the] dead I am being judged today by you.'"
en.B: I had been away for a number of years, and I came to bring charitable gifts to my people and to make offerings. \v 18 I was doing this when they found me in the temple, ritually purified, with no crowd around me and no disorder. \v 19 But some Jews from Asia were the ones who saw me. They should have come before you to accuse me, if they have any complaint against me. \v 20 Otherwise, let the men who are here tell you what wrong they discovered in me when I stood before the council, \v 21 unless it was the one sentence I called out as I stood among them: 'I am being judged by you today over the resurrection of the dead.'"
en.R: I had been away from Jerusalem for several years. Then I came back to bring money to help the poor among my people, and to offer gifts to God. \v 18 I was doing this when they found me in the temple. I had gone through the ceremony to make myself clean. There was no crowd with me, and I was not causing any trouble. \v 19 But some Jews from the province of Asia were there. They are the ones who should be here in front of you. If they have something against me, they should say so. \v 20 Or let these men who are here say what wrong I did when I stood in front of their council. \v 21 The only thing I did was call out one sentence while I stood there. I said, 'You are judging me today because I believe that the dead will rise.'"

es.L: Ahora bien, después de varios años vine para traer limosnas a mi nación, y ofrendas, \v 18 en medio de las cuales me encontraron purificado en el templo, no con multitud ni con alboroto. \v 19 Pero [había] unos judíos de Asia, que deberían estar presentes ante ti y acusar[me], si tuvieran algo contra mí. \v 20 O que estos mismos digan qué delito hallaron cuando comparecí ante el concilio, \v 21 salvo en cuanto a esta sola frase que grité estando en pie entre ellos: “Por [la] resurrección de [los] muertos estoy siendo juzgado hoy ante {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}”».
es.B: Después de varios años de ausencia, vine a traer donativos de caridad a mi pueblo y a presentar ofrendas. \v 18 En eso estaba cuando me encontraron en el templo, ya purificado, sin gente a mi alrededor y sin ningún desorden. \v 19 Pero los que me vieron fueron unos judíos de Asia. Ellos deberían haberse presentado ante ti para acusarme, si tienen alguna queja contra mí. \v 20 Si no, que los que están aquí digan qué delito encontraron en mí cuando comparecí ante el Consejo, \v 21 a no ser aquella única frase que grité estando entre ellos: “Hoy {{plural_you:ustedes me juzgan|vosotros me juzgáis}} por la resurrección de los muertos”».
es.R: Yo había estado lejos de Jerusalén durante varios años. Luego volví para traer dinero para ayudar a los pobres de mi pueblo, y para presentar ofrendas a Dios. \v 18 Estaba haciendo esto cuando me encontraron en el templo. Yo había pasado por la ceremonia para quedar puro. No había ninguna multitud conmigo, y yo no estaba causando ningún problema. \v 19 Pero allí había unos judíos de la provincia de Asia. Ellos son los que deberían estar aquí delante de ti. Si tienen algo contra mí, que lo digan. \v 20 O que estos hombres que están aquí digan qué mal hice cuando estuve delante de su Consejo Supremo. \v 21 Lo único que hice fue gritar una frase mientras estaba allí. Dije: “Hoy {{plural_you:ustedes me juzgan|vosotros me juzgáis}} porque creo que los muertos resucitarán”».

fr.L: Or, après plusieurs années, je suis venu apporter des aumônes à ma nation, et des offrandes, \v 18 au cours desquelles ils m’ont trouvé purifié dans le temple, ni avec une foule ni avec du tumulte. \v 19 Mais [il y avait] quelques Juifs d’Asie, qui devraient être présents devant toi et [m’]accuser, s’ils avaient quelque chose contre moi. \v 20 Ou bien, que ceux-ci eux-mêmes disent quel méfait ils ont trouvé quand j’ai comparu devant le Sanhédrin, \v 21 si ce n’est au sujet de cette seule parole que j’ai criée, debout au milieu d’eux : “C’est au sujet de la résurrection des morts que je suis jugé aujourd’hui par vous.” »
fr.B: Après plusieurs années d’absence, j’étais venu apporter des dons à mon peuple et présenter des offrandes. \v 18 C’est ce que je faisais quand on m’a trouvé dans le temple, rituellement purifié, sans foule autour de moi et sans aucun désordre. \v 19 Ce sont quelques Juifs d’Asie qui m’ont vu. C’est à eux qu’il revenait de se présenter devant toi pour m’accuser, s’ils ont quelque chose contre moi. \v 20 Sinon, que les hommes ici présents disent quelle faute ils ont découverte en moi quand j’ai comparu devant le Sanhédrin, \v 21 à moins qu’il ne s’agisse de cette seule phrase que j’ai lancée, debout au milieu d’eux : “C’est pour la résurrection des morts que je suis jugé aujourd’hui devant vous.” »
fr.R: J’avais été loin de Jérusalem pendant plusieurs années. Puis je suis revenu pour apporter de l’argent afin d’aider les pauvres de mon peuple, et pour offrir des dons à Dieu. \v 18 C’est ce que je faisais quand ils m’ont trouvé dans le temple. J’avais suivi la cérémonie pour me rendre pur. Il n’y avait pas de foule avec moi, et je ne causais aucun trouble. \v 19 Mais quelques Juifs de la province d’Asie étaient là. Ce sont eux qui devraient être ici, devant toi. S’ils ont quelque chose contre moi, ils devraient le dire. \v 20 Ou bien, que ces hommes qui sont ici disent quel mal j’ai fait quand j’étais debout devant leur grand conseil. \v 21 La seule chose que j’ai faite, c’est crier une phrase pendant que j’étais là. J’ai dit : “Vous me jugez aujourd’hui parce que je crois que les morts vont se relever.” »

sw.L: Basi baada ya miaka kadhaa nilikuja kuleta sadaka kwa taifa langu, na matoleo, \v 18 ambapo katika hayo walinikuta nimetakaswa hekaluni, si pamoja na umati wala pamoja na ghasia. \v 19 Lakini [walikuwepo] Wayahudi kadhaa kutoka Asia, ambao iliwapasa kuwapo mbele yako na kunishtaki, kama wangekuwa na neno lolote dhidi yangu. \v 20 Au hawa wenyewe na waseme ni kosa gani walilonikuta nalo niliposimama mbele ya baraza, \v 21 isipokuwa kuhusu sauti hii moja niliyoipaza nikiwa nimesimama kati yao, 'Kwa habari ya ufufuo wa wafu ninahukumiwa leo mbele yenu.'"
sw.B: Baada ya kukaa mbali kwa miaka kadhaa, nilikuja kuleta misaada kwa watu wa taifa langu na kutoa sadaka. \v 18 Nilikuwa nikifanya hivyo waliponikuta hekaluni, nikiwa nimekwisha kutakaswa kwa desturi, bila umati karibu nami na bila fujo yoyote. \v 19 Lakini walioniona ni Wayahudi fulani kutoka Asia. Hao ndio waliopaswa kufika mbele yako kunishtaki, kama wana lalamiko lolote dhidi yangu. \v 20 La sivyo, watu hawa walioko hapa na waseme ni kosa gani walilonikuta nalo niliposimama mbele ya baraza, \v 21 isipokuwa lile neno moja nililolitamka kwa sauti kubwa nikiwa nimesimama kati yao: 'Leo mnanihukumu kwa habari ya ufufuo wa wafu.'"
sw.R: Nilikuwa nimekaa mbali na Yerusalemu kwa miaka kadhaa. Kisha nikarudi kuleta fedha za kuwasaidia maskini wa watu wangu, na kumtolea Mungu sadaka. \v 18 Nilikuwa nikifanya hivyo waliponikuta hekaluni. Nilikuwa nimepitia ibada ya kujitakasa. Hapakuwa na umati pamoja nami, wala sikuwa nikifanya fujo yoyote. \v 19 Lakini kulikuwa na Wayahudi fulani kutoka jimbo la Asia. Wao ndio wanaopaswa kuwa hapa mbele yako. Kama wana jambo dhidi yangu, wanapaswa kulisema. \v 20 Au watu hawa walioko hapa waseme ni kosa gani nililofanya niliposimama mbele ya baraza kuu lao. \v 21 Jambo pekee nililofanya ni kusema neno moja kwa sauti kubwa nilipokuwa nimesimama pale. Nilisema, 'Leo mnanihukumu kwa sababu ninaamini kwamba wafu watafufuka.'"

decisions.choice: alms to my nation: gifts for the poor among the Jewish people
decisions.reason: Paul's letters tell of a collection he gathered from the churches for the poor believers in Jerusalem (Romans 15:25-28; 1 Corinthians 16:1-4; 2 Corinthians 8-9). This is probably what he means, the only mention of it in Acts. Before Felix he calls it simply alms for his nation.

decisions.choice: offerings: sacrifices presented in the temple
decisions.reason: The word is used of sacrifices. It may refer to the offerings for the vow in 21:23-26.

decisions.choice: purified: having gone through the rites of purification
decisions.reason: Paul had purified himself with four men under a vow before entering the temple (21:24, 21:26). So he was not defiling the temple, as the charge in 24:6 claimed.

decisions.choice: But some Jews from Asia: Paul breaks off his sentence
decisions.reason: The Greek begins a new subject and does not finish the clause about what these Jews did; it moves straight to where they should be now. Literal keeps the broken shape with supplied words.

decisions.choice: who ought to be present before you: the first accusers are missing
alternatives: they were not allowed to come
decisions.reason: The Jews from Asia started the riot (21:27). Roman practice expected accusers to face the accused in person (compare 25:16), and they had not come.

decisions.choice: the council: the Jewish high council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: This is the council of chief priests, elders and scribes before which Paul stood in 23:1-10.

decisions.choice: this one statement: Paul's cry in the council
decisions.reason: Paul quotes his own words in 23:6, which set the Pharisees and Sadducees against each other.

decisions.choice: charitable gifts
decisions.reason: "Alms" is old-fashioned; Balanced says what they were.

decisions.choice: because I believe that the dead will rise
alternatives: concerning the resurrection of the dead
decisions.reason: Readable says what the question about the resurrection was: whether the dead will rise, which Paul believed.

decisions.choice: el concilio (L); el Consejo (B); su Consejo Supremo (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide words for the Jewish high council in Jerusalem (meaning decision m6); Readable keeps "su", as the English "their council".

decisions.choice: limosnas (L); donativos de caridad (B); dinero para ayudar a los pobres (R); ofrendas at every level
decisions.reason: "Limosnas" is the old word for gifts to the poor (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say it in current words, as the English does. "Ofrendas" are the gifts brought to the temple (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: des aumônes (L); des dons (B)
decisions.reason: "Aumônes" is the exact word but now sounds churchy; Literal keeps it, Balanced says "dons" as the English says "charitable gifts", and Readable says what they were for (m1).

decisions.choice: sadaka (L), misaada (B), fedha za kuwasaidia maskini (R) for the alms; matoleo (L), sadaka (B, R) for the offerings
alternatives: sadaka for both at every level
decisions.reason: Two kinds of gift are meant: help for the poor of the nation (meaning decision m1) and offerings in the temple (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "sadaka", the usual word for alms, and "matoleo" for the offerings; Balanced and Readable keep "sadaka" for the temple offerings and say plainly that the first gift was help for the poor.

decisions.choice: baraza (L, B); baraza kuu (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the Jewish high council in Jerusalem (meaning decision m6); Readable adds "kuu" and keeps "lao", as the English "their council".

source.text: Ἀνεβάλετο δὲ αὐτοὺς ὁ Φῆλιξ, ἀκριβέστερον εἰδὼς τὰ περὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ, εἴπας· Ὅταν Λυσίας ὁ χιλίαρχος καταβῇ διαγνώσομαι τὰ καθ’ ὑμᾶς·

records.literal_gloss: Put off however them Felix, more accurately knowing the things concerning the Way, having said, When Lysias the tribune comes down, I will decide the things as to you;

en.L: But Felix, knowing rather accurately the things concerning the Way, put them off, saying, "When Lysias the tribune comes down, I will decide your case."
en.B: Felix knew a good deal about the Way, and he postponed the matter. He told them, "I will rule on your case once Lysias the tribune comes down."
en.R: Felix knew quite a lot about the Way. So he stopped the trial for the time being. He told them, "I will decide your case when Lysias comes down here." Lysias was the tribune who commanded the soldiers in Jerusalem.

es.L: Pero Félix, conociendo con bastante exactitud lo referente al Camino, los aplazó, diciendo: «Cuando Lisias el tribuno baje, decidiré {{plural_you:el caso de ustedes|vuestro caso}}».
es.B: Félix, que conocía bastante bien lo referente al Camino, aplazó el asunto. Les dijo: «Resolveré {{plural_you:el caso de ustedes|vuestro caso}} cuando baje el tribuno Lisias».
es.R: Félix sabía bastante sobre el Camino. Por eso suspendió el juicio por un tiempo. Les dijo: «Decidiré {{plural_you:el caso de ustedes|vuestro caso}} cuando Lisias venga aquí». Lisias era el tribuno que estaba al mando de los soldados en Jerusalén.

fr.L: Mais Félix, connaissant assez exactement ce qui concerne la Voie, les ajourna, disant : « Quand Lysias le tribun sera descendu, je statuerai sur votre affaire. »
fr.B: Félix, qui connaissait assez bien la Voie, renvoya l’affaire à plus tard. Il leur dit : « Je trancherai votre cas quand le tribun Lysias sera descendu. »
fr.R: Félix connaissait assez bien la Voie. Alors il a arrêté le procès pour le moment. Il leur a dit : « Je prendrai ma décision sur votre affaire quand Lysias sera descendu ici. » Lysias était le tribun qui commandait les soldats à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Lakini Feliki, akijua kwa usahihi zaidi mambo ya ile Njia, aliwaahirisha, akisema, "Lisia, yule kamanda, atakaposhuka, nitaamua shauri lenu."
sw.B: Feliki alikuwa akijua mambo mengi kuhusu ile Njia, naye akaahirisha shauri hilo. Akawaambia, "Nitatoa uamuzi juu ya shauri lenu Lisia, kamanda wa jeshi, atakaposhuka."
sw.R: Feliki alijua mambo mengi kuhusu ile Njia. Kwa hiyo aliisimamisha kesi kwa muda. Akawaambia, "Nitaamua kesi yenu Lisia atakapokuja hapa." Lisia alikuwa kamanda aliyewaongoza askari huko Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: put them off: adjourned the hearing
decisions.reason: The verb is a legal term for postponing a case to a later date.

decisions.choice: knowing rather accurately: knowing more than the accusers supposed
decisions.reason: The comparative may mean that Felix knew more about the Way than the speeches had shown, or simply that he was well informed. His wife Drusilla was Jewish (24:24), and believers had lived in Judea for years. Either way, he saw that the case was weak.

decisions.choice: Lysias the tribune: the Roman commander of the garrison in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: A tribune commanded a cohort of about a thousand soldiers. Claudius Lysias had arrested Paul and sent him to Felix (21:31-33; 23:26-30). Luke does not say that he ever came.

decisions.choice: Lysias was the tribune who commanded the soldiers in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title in a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: postponed the matter
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the plain legal sense of the verb.

decisions.choice: el tribuno, at every level
decisions.reason: Spanish has the Roman title, and Acts names the rank, as the English "tribune" does (meaning decision m3); Readable explains it, as the English Readable. "El caso de ustedes" avoids the ambiguous "su caso".

decisions.choice: kamanda
decisions.reason: As in John 18:12: the title means a Roman commander over a cohort (meaning decision m3). "Kamanda" is the plain modern word; "jemadari" is older and less widely understood. Readable explains it, as the English does.

source.text: διαταξάμενος τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ τηρεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἔχειν τε ἄνεσιν καὶ μηδένα κωλύειν τῶν ἰδίων αὐτοῦ ὑπηρετεῖν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: having ordered the centurion to keep him, to have then relief and no one to forbid of the own of him to serve him.

en.L: He ordered the centurion that he be kept [in custody] and have some relief, and that he forbid none of his own [people] to serve him.
en.B: He gave orders to the centurion: Paul was to stay in custody, but with some relief from strict confinement, and none of his own people were to be kept from helping him.
en.R: Felix told the centurion, an officer in charge of a hundred soldiers, to keep Paul under guard. But he told him to give Paul some freedom, and to let Paul's friends come and help him.

es.L: Y ordenó al centurión que él fuera custodiado y tuviera alivio, y que no impidiera a ninguno de los suyos servirlo.
es.B: Dio órdenes al centurión de que Pablo siguiera bajo custodia, pero con cierta libertad, y de que no se impidiera a ninguno de los suyos atenderlo.
es.R: Félix le dijo al centurión, un oficial al mando de cien soldados, que mantuviera a Pablo bajo vigilancia. Pero también le dijo que le diera a Pablo un poco de libertad y que dejara que sus amigos vinieran a ayudarlo.

fr.L: Il ordonna au centurion qu’il soit gardé et qu’il ait quelque liberté, et de n’empêcher aucun des siens de le servir.
fr.B: Il donna ses ordres au centurion : Paul resterait sous garde, mais avec un régime adouci, et on n’empêcherait aucun des siens de lui rendre service.
fr.R: Félix a dit au centurion, un officier qui commandait cent soldats, de garder Paul prisonnier. Mais il lui a dit de laisser à Paul un peu de liberté et de permettre à ses amis de venir l’aider.

sw.L: Akamwamuru akida kwamba alindwe, na awe na nafuu, na asimzuie yeyote wa watu wake mwenyewe kumhudumia.
sw.B: Akamwagiza akida kwamba Paulo aendelee kulindwa, lakini apewe nafuu kiasi, na asimzuie yeyote wa watu wake kumhudumia.
sw.R: Feliki alimwambia akida, afisa aliyeongoza askari mia moja, amweke Paulo chini ya ulinzi. Lakini alimwambia ampe Paulo uhuru kiasi, na awaruhusu rafiki zake waje kumsaidia.

decisions.choice: the sentence goes on: Felix is still the one acting
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT marks a pause after 24:22, and the participle "having ordered" goes on telling what Felix did.

decisions.choice: relief: lighter custody, some freedom
decisions.reason: The word means a loosening. Paul stayed a prisoner but was not held in strict confinement (compare 28:16, 28:30).

decisions.choice: his own: his friends and companions
decisions.reason: The phrase means those who belonged to him. They could bring him food and other things he needed, as friends did for prisoners.

decisions.choice: the centurion: a Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers
decisions.reason: Centurions served under the tribune and guarded Paul on the way to Caesarea (23:23).

decisions.choice: a new sentence beginning "He" or "Felix"
decisions.reason: A participle cannot open an English sentence, so each level starts a new sentence and names the subject.

decisions.choice: Paul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the prisoner.

decisions.choice: an officer in charge of a hundred soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title.

source.text: Μετὰ δὲ ἡμέρας τινὰς παραγενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ σὺν Δρουσίλλῃ τῇ ἰδίᾳ γυναικὶ οὔσῃ Ἰουδαίᾳ μετεπέμψατο τὸν Παῦλον καὶ ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ περὶ τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν πίστεως.

records.literal_gloss: After then days some having arrived Felix with Drusilla the own wife being a Jewess, he sent for Paul and heard him concerning the in Christ Jesus faith.

en.L: And after some days Felix came with Drusilla his wife, who was a Jewess, and he sent for Paul and heard him concerning faith in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.
en.B: A few days afterward Felix arrived with Drusilla, his wife, a Jewish woman. He had Paul brought in and heard what he had to say about faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.
en.R: A few days later, Felix came back with his wife Drusilla. She was Jewish. Felix sent for Paul and listened to him talk about having faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

es.L: Y después de algunos días, llegando Félix con Drusila, su propia esposa, que era judía, mandó llamar a Pablo y lo oyó acerca de la fe en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}.
es.B: Pocos días después llegó Félix con Drusila, su esposa, que era judía. Mandó traer a Pablo y escuchó lo que decía sobre la fe en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}.
es.R: Unos días después, Félix volvió con su esposa Drusila, que era judía. Félix mandó llamar a Pablo y lo escuchó hablar de cómo tener fe en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}.

fr.L: Et quelques jours après, Félix, étant arrivé avec Drusille sa femme, qui était juive, envoya chercher Paul et l’entendit au sujet de la foi au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus.
fr.B: Quelques jours plus tard, Félix vint avec Drusille, sa femme, qui était juive. Il fit venir Paul et l’écouta parler de la foi au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus.
fr.R: Quelques jours plus tard, Félix est revenu avec sa femme Drusille. Elle était juive. Félix a fait venir Paul et l’a écouté expliquer comment mettre sa foi en Jésus, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

sw.L: Na baada ya siku kadhaa Feliki akafika pamoja na Drusila mkewe mwenyewe, aliyekuwa Myahudi, akamwita Paulo, akamsikiliza kuhusu imani katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.B: Siku chache baadaye Feliki alikuja pamoja na mkewe Drusila, mwanamke Myahudi. Akamwita Paulo, akamsikiliza akizungumza juu ya imani katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.R: Siku chache baadaye, Feliki alirudi pamoja na mke wake Drusila. Yeye alikuwa Myahudi. Feliki alimwita Paulo, akamsikiliza akieleza jinsi ya kuwa na imani katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.

decisions.choice: Drusilla: a Jewish princess, daughter of King Herod Agrippa I
decisions.reason: Drusilla was a daughter of the Herod who died in 12:20-23 and a sister of Agrippa and Bernice (25:13). Josephus says she left her first husband to marry Felix (Antiquities 20.141-143).

decisions.choice: having arrived: Felix came back, or came to the hearing room
alternatives: Felix arrived in Caesarea for the first time
decisions.reason: Luke does not say where Felix had been. The point is that he came with Drusilla and then sent for Paul.

decisions.choice: faith in Christ Jesus: trust directed to Jesus as the Messiah
decisions.reason: The preposition shows where the faith is directed, as in 20:21 and 26:18.

decisions.choice: having faith in
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word faith and makes it an activity: trusting in Jesus.

decisions.choice: la foi au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus (L, B); Jésus, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (R)
decisions.reason: French keeps the Greek order "Christ Jésus" at Literal and Balanced; the contraction "au" lets both options read naturally ("au Christ Jésus", "au Messie Jésus"). Readable puts the title after the name in apposition, which is plainer.

source.text: διαλεγομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ περὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ ἐγκρατείας καὶ τοῦ κρίματος τοῦ μέλλοντος ἔμφοβος γενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ ἀπεκρίθη· Τὸ νῦν ἔχον πορεύου, καιρὸν δὲ μεταλαβὼν μετακαλέσομαί σε·

records.literal_gloss: Reasoning then him concerning righteousness and self-control and the judgment the coming, afraid having become Felix answered, The for now go, opportunity then having found I will summon you;

en.L: And as he reasoned about righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment, Felix became afraid and answered, "Go for the present, and when I find an opportunity I will summon you."
en.B: As Paul reasoned with him about righteousness, self-control and the judgment that is coming, Felix became alarmed. "Leave me for now," he answered. "I will call for you again when I find a suitable time."
en.R: Paul talked about righteousness, about controlling yourself, and about the day when God will judge everyone. Felix became afraid. He said, "Go away for now. When I have time, I will call for you again."

es.L: Y mientras él razonaba sobre la justicia, el dominio de sí y el juicio que había de venir, Félix, lleno de temor, respondió: «Por el momento vete; y cuando encuentre ocasión, te haré llamar».
es.B: Mientras Pablo le hablaba de la justicia, del dominio de sí mismo y del juicio que ha de venir, Félix se alarmó. «Déjame por ahora», le respondió. «Te volveré a llamar cuando encuentre un momento oportuno».
es.R: Pablo habló de la justicia, de saber controlarse y del día en que Dios juzgará a todos. Félix tuvo miedo y le dijo: «Vete por ahora. Cuando tenga tiempo, te volveré a llamar».

fr.L: Et comme il discourait sur la justice, la maîtrise de soi et le jugement à venir, Félix, devenu craintif, répondit : « Pour l’instant, va ; et quand j’aurai l’occasion, je te convoquerai. »
fr.B: Comme Paul l’entretenait de la justice, de la maîtrise de soi et du jugement qui vient, Félix prit peur. « Laisse-moi pour aujourd’hui, répondit-il. Je te ferai rappeler quand je trouverai un moment favorable. »
fr.R: Paul a parlé de la justice, de savoir se contrôler, et du jour où Dieu jugera tout le monde. Félix a eu peur. Il a dit : « Va-t’en pour le moment. Quand j’aurai le temps, je te ferai revenir. »

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akijadiliana kuhusu haki na kujizuia na hukumu inayokuja, Feliki akawa na hofu, akajibu, "Kwa wakati huu ondoka; nami nitakapopata wakati unaofaa nitakuagiza uje."
sw.B: Paulo alipokuwa akijadiliana naye kuhusu haki, kujizuia na hukumu inayokuja, Feliki alishtuka. Akamjibu, "Niache kwa sasa. Nitakuita tena nitakapopata wakati unaofaa."
sw.R: Paulo alizungumza kuhusu haki, kuhusu kujizuia, na kuhusu siku ambayo Mungu atawahukumu watu wote. Feliki akaogopa. Akasema, "Nenda kwa sasa. Nitakapopata muda, nitakuita tena."

decisions.choice: righteousness: the right conduct that God requires
alternatives: God's gift of being made right with him
decisions.reason: Next to self-control and judgment, the word here means living justly, as God demands. Felix was known for injustice, and he had taken another man's wife.

decisions.choice: self-control: mastery over one's desires
decisions.reason: The word means command of oneself, especially over desires (Galatians 5:23).

decisions.choice: the coming judgment: God's judgment of all people
decisions.reason: Paul preached that God has fixed a day when he will judge the world (17:31).

decisions.choice: an opportunity: a convenient time
decisions.reason: The word means a fitting time. Felix puts Paul off until it suits him.

decisions.choice: the day when God will judge everyone
decisions.reason: Readable says whose judgment it is and whom it concerns, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: controlling yourself
decisions.reason: Readable uses a verb in place of an abstract noun.

decisions.choice: la justice at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for righteousness; here it means the right conduct God requires (m1), which "la justice" carries in French. Readable keeps it, as the English Readable keeps "righteousness".

decisions.choice: kujizuia
decisions.reason: The word is mastery over one's own desires (meaning decision m2). "Kujizuia" says that; "kiasi" is kept for the sensible moderation of the Pastoral letters.

source.text: ἅμα καὶ ἐλπίζων ὅτι χρήματα δοθήσεται αὐτῷ ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου· διὸ καὶ πυκνότερον αὐτὸν μεταπεμπόμενος ὡμίλει αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: At the same time also hoping that money will be given to him by Paul; therefore also more often him sending for he was conversing with him.

en.L: At the same time he was also hoping that money would be given to him by Paul; therefore he also sent for him rather often and conversed with him.
en.B: At the same time he hoped for money from Paul, so he had him brought in quite often and talked with him.
en.R: Felix also hoped that Paul would give him money to let him go free. So he often sent for Paul and talked with him.

es.L: A la vez esperaba también que Pablo le diera dinero; por eso también lo hacía venir con bastante frecuencia y conversaba con él.
es.B: Al mismo tiempo esperaba que Pablo le diera dinero, así que lo hacía traer muy a menudo y hablaba con él.
es.R: Félix también esperaba que Pablo le diera dinero para dejarlo libre. Por eso lo mandaba llamar a menudo y hablaba con él.

fr.L: En même temps, il espérait aussi que de l’argent lui serait donné par Paul ; c’est pourquoi aussi, le faisant venir assez souvent, il s’entretenait avec lui.
fr.B: Il espérait en même temps que Paul lui donnerait de l’argent ; aussi le faisait-il venir assez souvent pour s’entretenir avec lui.
fr.R: Félix espérait aussi que Paul allait lui donner de l’argent pour être libéré. C’est pour cela qu’il faisait souvent venir Paul pour parler avec lui.

sw.L: Wakati huo huo alikuwa akitumaini pia kwamba atapewa fedha na Paulo; kwa hiyo pia alikuwa akimwita mara kwa mara zaidi na kuzungumza naye.
sw.B: Wakati huo huo alitumaini kwamba Paulo angempa fedha, kwa hiyo alikuwa akimwita mara nyingi na kuzungumza naye.
sw.R: Feliki pia alitumaini kwamba Paulo angempa fedha ili amwachilie huru. Kwa hiyo alimwita mara nyingi na kuzungumza naye.

decisions.choice: money: a bribe for Paul's release
decisions.reason: Roman law forbade governors to take money from those on trial, but the practice was common. Felix may have heard of the funds Paul had brought (24:17).

decisions.choice: rather often: quite frequently
decisions.reason: The comparative here means simply "fairly often".

decisions.choice: to let him go free
decisions.reason: Readable says what the money would be for, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: Διετίας δὲ πληρωθείσης ἔλαβεν διάδοχον ὁ Φῆλιξ Πόρκιον Φῆστον· θέλων τε χάριτα καταθέσθαι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὁ Φῆλιξ κατέλιπε τὸν Παῦλον δεδεμένον.

records.literal_gloss: Two years however having been completed, received successor Felix Porcius Festus; wishing then favor to lay up with the Jews Felix left Paul bound.

en.L: But when two years had been completed, Felix received a successor, Porcius Festus; and wishing to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul bound.
en.B: Two full years went by, and then Porcius Festus succeeded Felix. Felix wished to earn the favor of the Jews, so he left Paul behind in chains.
en.R: Two years later, a man named Porcius Festus took Felix's place as governor. Felix wanted to win the favor of the Jewish leaders, so he left Paul in prison.

es.L: Y habiéndose cumplido dos años, Félix tuvo por sucesor a Porcio Festo; y deseando ganarse el favor de los judíos, Félix dejó a Pablo encadenado.
es.B: Pasaron dos años completos, y Porcio Festo sucedió a Félix. Como Félix quería ganarse el favor de los judíos, dejó allí a Pablo encadenado.
es.R: Dos años después, un hombre llamado Porcio Festo ocupó el lugar de Félix como gobernador. Félix quería quedar bien con los dirigentes judíos, así que dejó a Pablo en la cárcel.

fr.L: Mais deux années s’étant écoulées, Félix reçut pour successeur Porcius Festus ; et voulant s’attirer la faveur des Juifs, Félix laissa Paul enchaîné.
fr.B: Deux années entières passèrent, puis Porcius Festus succéda à Félix. Comme Félix voulait gagner les bonnes grâces des Juifs, il laissa Paul derrière lui, dans les chaînes.
fr.R: Deux ans plus tard, un homme appelé Porcius Festus a remplacé Félix comme gouverneur. Félix voulait plaire aux chefs juifs, alors il a laissé Paul en prison.

sw.L: Lakini miaka miwili ilipotimia, Feliki alipata mrithi, Porkio Festo; na akitaka kujipatia fadhila kwa Wayahudi, Feliki alimwacha Paulo akiwa amefungwa.
sw.B: Miaka miwili ilipotimia, Porkio Festo alichukua nafasi ya Feliki. Feliki alitaka kujipatia fadhila kwa Wayahudi, kwa hiyo akamwacha Paulo akiwa amefungwa minyororo.
sw.R: Miaka miwili baadaye, mtu mmoja aitwaye Porkio Festo alichukua nafasi ya Feliki kuwa mkuu wa mkoa. Feliki alitaka viongozi wa Wayahudi wampende, kwa hiyo akamwacha Paulo gerezani.

decisions.choice: favor: goodwill from people, not the grace of God
decisions.reason: The word usually means God's grace, but here it is human goodwill, which Felix hoped to store up with the Jewish leaders (compare 25:3, 25:9). The same sense appears in 7:10 and 7:46.

decisions.choice: two years: the time Paul spent in custody in Caesarea
decisions.reason: The two years most naturally count Paul's imprisonment from 24:23. They are not the whole time Felix was governor.

decisions.choice: Porcius Festus: the next Roman governor of Judea
decisions.reason: Josephus tells that Felix was recalled to Rome after complaints from the Jews of Caesarea and that Festus took his place (Antiquities 20.182). Festus died in office after a short rule.

decisions.choice: to gain favor: to lay up goodwill for himself
alternatives: to do the Jews a kindness
decisions.reason: The verb means to deposit or store up. Felix wanted the Jewish leaders to owe him something as he left office.

decisions.choice: bound: in custody, a prisoner
decisions.reason: The word means bound, and Paul was in chains (26:29), though with some freedom (24:23).

decisions.choice: took Felix's place as governor
decisions.reason: Readable says what office Festus took.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Readable names the people whose goodwill Felix wanted: the leaders who had accused Paul.

decisions.choice: fadhila
decisions.reason: Here the word is goodwill won from people, not the grace of God (meaning decision m1), so it is not "neema", the book-wide word for grace.
